findings.description: The change drops the per-waiter Deferred and awaits the shared parser Deferred directly. A Deferred holds a single callback chain. When several requests for the same netloc await it at once, maybe_deferred_to_future adds a callback to the shared Deferred that returns None. The first waiter gets the RobotParser, but the next waiter's callback receives None. Any request after the first therefore sees rp=None, so process_request_2 skips the robots.txt check and the request is allowed even if it is disallowed. A second effect is that the shared Deferred can end up holding a non-parser result for anyone who awaits it later.
findings.suggestion: Restore a per-waiter Deferred that is fed from the shared one through a callback that returns the result unchanged, as in the removed code. Alternatively, store an asyncio.Future or an event and give every waiter the same result.
findings.title: Multiple waiters share one Deferred, so later waiters get a wrong result
